Values of a Profile

Source: R/profile.R
profile_range.Rd

Selects the values at which statmod_profile() evaluates the profile of a coefficient: n equally spaced values from width standard errors below the estimate to width standard errors above it, on the scale of the coefficient in the linear predictor.

Usage

profile_range(width = 3, n = 21, fallback = 3)

ProfileRange(width = integer(0), n = integer(0), fallback = 3)

Arguments

width

A single positive number: the half-width of the grid in standard errors.

n

A single integer, at least 2: the number of values.

fallback

A single positive number: the half-width of the grid of a hyperparameter on the scale of its link, used where its standard error is not available.

Value

An object of class ProfileRange, with the properties width, n and fallback.

Details

The standard error is the one of vcov(fit), so it follows the variance convention that vcov() uses by default. The grid is symmetric about the estimate, and it contains the estimate itself when n is odd.

For a hyperparameter the grid is placed on the scale of its link (for example \(\log\lambda\)), at the estimate plus and minus width standard errors, with the standard error from the exact Hessian of the outer criterion, the one that summary() reads. Where that standard error is not available, or the estimate lies outside the interval below, because the hyperparameter is at an edge of its range or the criterion is flat in its direction, the grid is the estimate, cut to that interval, plus and minus fallback. The values are cut to the interval from -8 to 8 of the scale of the link, which statmod_certificate() reads as the interior.

The scale is the unconstrained one. A coefficient of a linear predictor lives there, and so do the parameters of a nonlinear term, the positions of the break-points and the parameters of a covariance structure; the scale of the coefficients is described at statmod_profile().

See also

statmod_profile(), which takes it in its argument values.

Examples

profile_range()
#> <statmodels7::ProfileRange>
#>  @ width   : num 3
#>  @ n       : int 21
#>  @ fallback: num 3
profile_range(width = 2, n = 9)
#> <statmodels7::ProfileRange>
#>  @ width   : num 2
#>  @ n       : int 9
#>  @ fallback: num 3
